messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: refactoring includes
parts:
I'm trying to do a couple of things to get the
includes under control.

1. Eliminating using at namespace or file level.

2. Add a test for each standalone file to make
sure it compiles.

3. Get rid of includes that aren't being used.

Turns out we were leaning on lots of accidental
includes many includes deep, many of which are now
cleaned up.

The remaining trouble spot is the distribution
and matrix stuff.

I was only partly successful in replacing direct
use of Eigen with typedefs. I'm sure it's fixable
with a little more scrutiny.

The tests now officially take forever to run
on my notebook. I'm 11 minutes in and still
going before I commit using clang++ (2.9 still)
and -O0. And there are actually fewer includes.
I found and eliminated lots of useless ones.

Ah, 18 minutes end to end. But it works.

- Bob

Do you not use make -j# to build in parallel?

With g++, I get

time make -j5 all > /dev/null

...

real 4m28.555s
user 18m23.035s
sys 0m36.687s

I can only use 5 (virtual) cores with g++ because more would spike RAM
over 8GB.

With clang++ the RAM stays under 6GB even using all 8 (virtual) cores:

time make -j8 all > /dev/null

...

real 1m46.302s
user 12m34.018s
sys 0m28.234s

YMMV,
Ben
